decisions.reason: Report distinguishes the clipboard-text projection (InputState.draft, Occurrence.offset/length, chips expanded to clipboardText) from the detect projection (EditorProjection.detectText, chip = one U+FFFC) used by insertReference/consumeToken, citing host-input-contract.ts and the facade, and shows separator/text width via the 29-vs-2 length comparison.

Locates snapshot.draft.length as the span source in add (plugin-client.js:28–31); explains that with an empty composer [0,0) is valid in both coordinate systems so paste #1 succeeds, while paste #2 sends [29,29) into a 2-char detect document, the splice fails, insertReference returns false, and the plugin emits its changed-composer toast — explicitly noting the toast is a misdiagnosis, not a real concurrent edit.

Traces remove passing occurrence.offset/length unconverted as a [0,28) span to consumeToken, the splice failing over the 2-char detect document, the false return ignored while records.delete and changed() run anyway, leaving the live occurrence with the composer chip intact while the missing record renders 'unavailable'; ties both symptoms to the same coordinate mismatch.

Derives toDetect(x) = x − Σ(occ.length − 1) from the contract excerpts with a sanity check, applies it at the insert call site (fresh snapshot, revision guard and rollback kept) and at removal (mapped offset plus a one-detect-character span), and retires the record only when consumeToken returns true.

Plan A asserts two successive pastes with both chips/occurrences present; Plan B removes a chip while another survives, asserting composer occurrence, dock chip and record are removed together, and adds declined-consumption (stale-rev, record kept) and remove-last/empty-again variants.
